claim: Adipoq is most highly expressed in the MSPC-adipo (mesenchymal progenitor cells-adipo lineage)/Adipoq-lineage progenitors cluster among bone marrow cells.
source: Adipoq is found to be most highly expressed in the cluster MSPC-adipo (mesenchymal progenitor cells-adipo lineage)/Adipoq-lineage progenitors (Figure 1A, B and D) as a marker of this cell population among the clusters.
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data analysis shown in Figure 1 and described in the text.

claim: Bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors are relatively quiescent, with about 4% cells incorporating BrdU under basal conditions.
source: These cells labeled by Adipoq Cre were relatively quiescent, with about 4% cells incorporating BrdU under basal conditions (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by BrdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Adipoq-lineage progenitors are not mature adipocytes but express some common adipocyte lineage markers such as Cebpa and Adipoq.
source: The Adipoq-lineage progenitors are not mature adipocytes, but express some common adipocyte lineage markers, such as Cebpa and Adipoq (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Osteoblast lineage marker genes such as Sp7, Alpl, Dmp1, and Bglap are nearly undetectable in Adipoq-lineage progenitors.
source: On the other hand, osteoblast lineage marker genes, such as Sp7, Alpl, Dmp1, and Bglap, are nearly undetectable in these cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors (MSPC-adipo cluster) express the highest level of Csf1 among bone marrow cells.
source: When screening expression of known genes regulating skeletal homeostasis in the bone marrow, we found that these bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors (MSPC-adipo cluster) express the highest level of Csf1 (Figure 1D, E and F), which was unexpected because the MSPC-osteo (mesenchymal progenitor cells-osteo lineage) cluster and osteoblasts were thought to be the cellular source expressing Csf1 in bone marrow based on previous studies of in vitro cultured osteoblast cell lines or calvarial osteoblastic cells (Tanaka et al., 1993; Elford et al., 1987).
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data analysis shown in Figure 1D, E, and F, and referenced to previous studies.

claim: Bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors express markedly higher levels of Csf1 than MSPC-osteo cluster cells (70% of 6441 cells with scaled average expression level at 2.6 vs 61% of 2247 cells with scaled average expression level at 1.3).
source: Further quantitative analysis showed that bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors (70% of 6441 cells expressed with scaled average expression level at 2.6) express a markedly higher level of Csf1 than MSPC-osteo cluster cells (61% of 2247 cells expressed with scaled average expression level at 1.3) (Figure 1E, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by quantitative scRNAseq data analysis shown in Figure 1E and source data.

claim: Csf1 expression is negligible in osteo cluster and osteoblasts (scaled average expression level at 0).
source: Csf1 expression was negligible in osteo cluster and osteoblasts (scaled average expression level at 0, Figure 1E, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data analysis shown in Figure 1E and source data.

claim: Human bone marrow contains a cell population (cluster 1, Adipoq-lineage progenitors) that expresses high ADIPOQ, bone marrow stromal marker genes LEPR, CXCL12 and KITLG, LPL and CEBPA, but with nearly undetectable osteoblast lineage genes.
source: We analyzed a recently published scRNAseq dataset based on human femur bone marrow (Wang et al., 2021), and identified a similar cell population (cluster 1, Adipoq-lineage progenitors) that expressed high ADIPOQ, bone marrow stromal marker genes LEPR, CXCL12 and KITLG, LPL and CEBPA, but with nearly undetectable osteoblast lineage genes (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by analysis of human scRNAseq data shown in Figure 2A and B, and referenced to Wang et al., 2021.

claim: The human bone marrow stromal cell population (cluster 1, Adipoq-lineage progenitors) is most highly enriched in CSF1 expression across the clusters.
source: This cell population was mostly highly enriched in CSF1 expression across the clusters (Figure 2C, D and E).
evidence: Supported by human scRNAseq data analysis shown in Figure 2C, D, and E.

claim: Human bone marrow contains a cell population highly similar to the bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors in mice with conserved robust expression of CSF1.
source: These results indicate that human bone marrow contains a cell population that is highly similar to the bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors in mice with conserved robust expression of CSF1.
evidence: Inferred from the analysis of human scRNAseq datasets showing similar cell populations expressing ADIPOQ and CSF1.

claim: The mRNA expression of Csf1 in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitor cells is 20-30 fold higher than that of mature adipocytes.
source: We found that the mRNA expression of Csf1 in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitor cells is 20–30 fold higher than that of mature adipocytes (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Csf1 expression in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitor cells is much higher than that of the stromal vascular fraction (SVF) cells in white adipose.
source: The Csf1 expression in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitor cells is also much higher than that of the stromal vascular fraction (SVF) cells in white adipose (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The majority of bone marrow Adipoq-expressing progenitor cells express M-CSF (93.2%, 1865 cells out of 2001 cells counted, n=3 mice).
source: We observed that the majority of bone marrow Adipoq-expressing progenitor cells express M-CSF (Figure 3B, 1865 cells out of 2001 cells counted, n=3 mice, 93.2%).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: M-CSF expression is not detected in mature bone marrow adipocytes (Perilipin1+) (0 cells out of 115 cells counted, n=3 mice, 0%).
source: In contrast, M-CSF expression was not detected in mature bone marrow adipocytes (Perilipin1+) (Figure 3C, 0 cells out of 115 cells counted, n=3 mice, 0%), indicating that mature bone marrow adipocytes are unlikely to be a significant source of M-CSF.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The stromal vascular fraction (SVF) cells in adipose express M-CSF.
source: As shown in Figure 3D, the stromal vascular fraction (SVF) cells in adipose, which contain multiple cell populations including adipogenic progenitors, express M-CSF.
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: M-CSF is nearly undetectable in peripheral mature adipocytes isolated from inguinal and epididymal white adipose tissue (WAT).
source: On the contrary, M-CSF was nearly undetectable in the peripheral mature adipocytes isolated from inguinal and epididymal white adipose tissue (WAT) (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Mature adipocytes are not a significant source of M-CSF as evidenced by nearly undetectable M-CSF expression compared to the Adipoq-lineage progenitors.
source: These data collectively support that mature adipocytes are not a significant source of M-CSF as evidenced by nearly undetectable M-CSF expression compared to the Adipoq-lineage progenitors.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing low or undetectable M-CSF in mature adipocytes.

claim: Adipoq-lineage progenitors residing in bone marrow are a new cell type highly expressing M-CSF.
source: These results identify Adipoq-lineage progenitors residing in bone marrow as a new cell type highly expressing M-CSF.
evidence: Inferred from the collective experimental data showing high M-CSF expression in Adipoq-lineage progenitors.

claim: Csf1 expression is reduced by approximately 75% in total bone marrow stromal cell culture derived from Csf1∆Adipoq mice compared to control mice.
source: Compared to control mice, Csf1 expression was reduced by approximately 75% in a total bone marrow stromal cell culture derived from the Csf1∆Adipoq mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors constitute only about 0.08% of bone marrow cells.
source: Given that bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors constitute only about 0.08% of bone marrow cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), these results, together with the data shown in Figures 1—3, support that bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors are the major cellular source of M-CSF expression in the bone marrow.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors are the major cellular source of M-CSF expression in the bone marrow.
source: Given that bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors constitute only about 0.08% of bone marrow cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), these results, together with the data shown in Figures 1—3, support that bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors are the major cellular source of M-CSF expression in the bone marrow.
evidence: Inferred from the combination of low cell percentage but high M-CSF expression and the 75% reduction in Csf1 expression in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.

claim: Immunofluorescence staining of bone slices shows a drastic decrease in M-CSF protein expression in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitor cells in Csf1∆Adipoq mice compared to control mice.
source: Furthermore, immunofluorescence staining of bone slices showed a drastic decrease in M-CSF protein expression in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitor cells in Csf1∆Adipoq mice compared to the control mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Csf1 expression in SVF is not altered in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: Indeed, our results showed that Csf1 expression in SVF was not altered in Csf1∆Adipoq mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Adipoq-cre does not target SVF cells.
source: These results clearly demonstrate that adipoq-cre does not target SVF cells.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Csf1 expression in SVF is unchanged in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.

claim: The deficiency of Csf1 in Csf1∆Adipoq mice does not affect the expression of Il34, Il1b, Il6, Il10, Csf2, Tnf, and Cxcl12 in bone marrow.
source: We also examined the expression of a group of cytokines that often regulate macrophage function and osteoclastogenesis in bone marrow, including Il34, Il1b, Il6, Il10, Csf2, Tnf, Cxcl12, and found that the deficiency of Csf1 in Csf1∆Adipoq mice did not affect the expression of these genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Csf1∆Adipoq mice do not display abnormalities in gross appearance, body weight, tooth eruption and long bone length.
source: Csf1∆Adipoq mice did not display abnormalities in gross appearance, body weight, tooth eruption and long bone length (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by phenotypic observations and measurements shown in Figure 4C, D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Csf1∆Adipoq mice exhibit a marked osteopetrotic phenotype, as indicated by a twofold increase in trabecular bone mass and marked increases in bone mineral density (BMD), connectivity density (Conn-Dens.), trabecular bone number and a decrease in trabecular bone spacing compared to littermate control mice.
source: In contrast, microcomputed tomographic (µCT) analyses showed that Csf1∆Adipoq mice exhibited a marked osteopetrotic phenotype, as indicated by a twofold increase in trabecular bone mass and marked increases in bone mineral density (BMD), connectivity density (Conn-Dens.), trabecular bone number and a decrease in trabecular bone spacing compared to the littermate control mice (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: Cortical bone appears normal in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: Cortical bone appeared normal in Csf1∆Adipoq mice (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Heterozygous Csf1 conditional knockout mice (Csf1f/+;Adipoq Cre) do not show an abnormal bone phenotype compared to control mice (Csf1f/f).
source: In addition, heterozygous Csf1 conditional knockout mice (Csf1f/+;Adipoq Cre) did not show an abnormal bone phenotype compared to control mice (Csf1f/f) (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: There are no differences in vertebral BMD or bone mass between the control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: There are no differences in vertebral BMD or bone mass between the control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: Csf1 in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors plays a key role in the bone mass maintenance of long bones.
source: Given that peripheral mature adipocytes (Adipoq + cells in peripheral adipose tissue) and mature bone marrow adipocytes (Adipoq +lipid-laden cells in bone marrow) express negligible levels of M-CSF, these data indicate that Csf1 in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors plays a key role in the bone mass maintenance of long bones.
evidence: Inferred from the osteopetrotic phenotype in Csf1∆Adipoq mice and the negligible M-CSF expression in mature adipocytes.

claim: Csf1 deficiency in Adipoq+ cells impairs osteoclast formation in vivo as evidenced by reduced osteoclast surface area and lower osteoclast numbers.
source: Indeed, Csf1 deficiency in Adipoq+ cells impaired osteoclast formation in vivo evidenced by reduced osteoclast surface area and lower osteoclast numbers (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by TRAP staining and histomorphometric analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The TRAP level in serum is significantly lower in Csf1∆Adipoq mice than in control mice.
source: The TRAP level in serum was significantly lower in Csf1∆Adipoq mice than that in control mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by ELISA analysis data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Mineral apposition rate (MAR) and bone formation rate (BFR) are not affected in Csf1∆Adipoq mice, indicating normal osteoblastic function in these mice.
source: On the other hand, mineral apposition rate (MAR) and bone formation rate (BFR) were not affected in Csf1∆Adipoq mice, indicating normal osteoblastic function in these mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by dynamic histomorphometric analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: CD11b+Ly6Chi monocytes are similar between control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: CD11b+Ly6 Chi monocytes were similar between control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data described in the text.

claim: CD11b+F4/80+ macrophages are reduced by almost half in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: CD11b+F4/80+macrophages were reduced by almost half in Csf1∆Adipoq mice (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The decrease in macrophages in Csf1∆Adipoq mice reflects the effects of M-CSF deficiency, as M-CSF is critical for macrophage development.
source: This decrease in macrophages reflects the effects of M-CSF deficiency, as M-CSF is critical for macrophage development.
evidence: Inferred from the known role of M-CSF in macrophage development and the observed reduction in macrophages.

claim: The inflammatory response of BMMs, indicated by inflammatory gene induction and the activation of MAPK or NF-κB pathways in response to LPS, is similar between the BMMs derived from the control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: We further stimulated bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs) with LPS and found that the inflammatory response of BMMs, indicated by inflammatory gene induction (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A) and the activation of MAPK or NF-κB pathways in response to LPS (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B), was similar between the BMMs derived from the control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and 2B.

claim: RANKL can induce osteoclast differentiation in control bone marrow cultures even without addition of M-CSF, but it fails to induce osteoclastogenesis in Csf1∆Adipoq bone marrow culture.
source: As shown in Figure 5D, RANKL can induce osteoclast differentiation in the control bone marrow cultures even without addition of M-CSF, but it failed to induce osteoclastogenesis in the Csf1∆Adipoq bone marrow culture.
evidence: Supported by osteoclast differentiation assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: When recombinant M-CSF is added back to the bone marrow cultures, the osteoclast formation in Csf1∆Adipoq cell cultures is similar to that in the control cultures.
source: When recombinant M-CSF was added back to the bone marrow cultures, the osteoclast formation in Csf1∆Adipoq cell cultures was similar to that in the control cultures (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by osteoclast differentiation assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The M-CSF secreted by bone marrow resident Adipoq-lineage progenitors is critical for osteoclastogenesis.
source: These results demonstrate that the M-CSF secreted by bone marrow resident Adipoq-lineage progenitors is critical for osteoclastogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the osteoclast differentiation assay results showing failure of osteoclastogenesis in Csf1∆Adipoq bone marrow without exogenous M-CSF.

claim: The gross appearance and weight of the spleen and peripheral adipose tissue, including the inguinal and epididymal adipose depots, are normal in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: The gross appearance and weight of the spleen and peripheral adipose tissue, including the inguinal and epididymal adipose depots, were normal in Csf1∆Adipoq mice (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Supported by phenotypic observations and weight measurements shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: There is no difference in CD11b+Ly6Chi monocytes in the spleen, inguinal or epididymal adipose tissue between control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: There was no difference in CD11b+Ly6 Chi monocytes in either the spleen, inguinal or epididymal adipose tissue between control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice, and the amount of CD11b+F4/80+macrophages was unchanged in these tissues (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The amount of CD11b+F4/80+ macrophages is unchanged in the spleen, inguinal or epididymal adipose tissue in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: There was no difference in CD11b+Ly6 Chi monocytes in either the spleen, inguinal or epididymal adipose tissue between control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice, and the amount of CD11b+F4/80+macrophages was unchanged in these tissues (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Csf1 deficiency in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors does not influence macrophage development in peripheral adipose tissue or the spleen.
source: Thus, in contrast to the effects on bone marrow macrophages, Csf1 deficiency in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors does not influence macrophage development in peripheral adipose tissue or the spleen.
evidence: Inferred from the flow cytometry data showing no change in macrophage populations in these tissues.

claim: Uterine weights are decreased approximately 75% in OVX groups compared with the sham group, indicating comparable and effective estrogen depletion in both control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: Uterine weights were decreased approximately 75% in OVX groups compared with the sham group (Figure 7A), indicating comparable and effective estrogen depletion in both control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
evidence: Supported by uterine weight measurements shown in Figure 7A.

claim: OVX does not alter Csf1 expression in the bone marrow.
source: OVX did not alter Csf1 expression in the bone marrow (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: OVX significantly reduces bone mass indicated by a decrease in BV/TV, trabecular number, trabecular thickness, Conn-Dens. and an increase of trabecular spacing compared with the sham group in the control mice.
source: μCT analysis showed that OVX significantly reduced bone mass indicated by a decrease in BV/TV, trabecular number, trabecular thickness, Conn-Dens. and an increase of trabecular spacing compared with the sham group in the control mice (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: OVX decreases the bone mass of Csf1∆Adipoq mice, but the extent of bone loss is less than that of control mice.
source: Although OVX also decreased the bone mass of Csf1∆Adipoq mice, the extent of bone loss was less than that of control mice (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: Significant changes are identified between the control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice in several μCT parameters after OVX: a decrease in trabecular BV/TV (35.1% in the control vs 20.9% in Csf1∆Adipoq mice), a decrease in Tb.N (11.34% in the control vs 7.97% in Csf1∆Adipoq mice), a decrease in Conn-Dens (39.7% in the control vs 14.56% in Csf1∆Adipoq mice), and an increase in Tb.Sp (12.51% in the control vs 1.97% in Csf1∆Adipoq mice).
source: Significant changes were identified between the control and Csf1∆Adipoq mice in several μCT parameters. For example, a decrease in trabecular BV/TV after OVX: 35.1% in the control vs 20.9% in Csf1∆Adipoq mice; a decrease in Tb. N after OVX:11.34% in the control vs 7.97% in Csf1∆Adipoq mice; a decrease in Conn-Dens after OVX: 39.7% in the control vs 14.56% in Csf1∆Adipoq mice; an increase in Tb. Sp after OVX: 12.51% in the control vs 1.97% in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data described in the text.

claim: The bone mass is markedly higher in Csf1∆Adipoq mice than control mice after OVX, indicating a significant role for the M-CSF secreted by Adipoq+ cells in estrogen-deficiency induced bone loss.
source: Furthermore, the bone mass was markedly higher in Csf1∆Adipoq mice than control mice after OVX (Figure 7B and C, column 4 vs 2), indicating a significant role for the M-CSF secreted by Adipoq + cells in estrogen-deficiency induced bone loss.
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: Osteoclast formation as indicated by osteoclast surface and numbers is significantly enhanced by OVX in control mice.
source: OVX is an osteoclastogenic stimulus. Thus, osteoclast formation as indicated by osteoclast surface and numbers was significantly enhanced by OVX in control mice (Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by TRAP staining and histomorphometric analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Bone histomorphometric analysis shows significantly greater osteoclast numbers and surface area in control mice with OVX than Csf1∆Adipoq mice with OVX.
source: Bone histomorphometric analysis further showed significantly greater osteoclast numbers and surface area in control mice with OVX than Csf1∆Adipoq mice with OVX (Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by histomorphometric analysis data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Despite an increase in osteoclast surface in Csf1∆Adipoq mice after OVX, osteoclast numbers are not significantly influenced by OVX.
source: Despite an increase in osteoclast surface in Csf1∆Adipoq mice after OVX, osteoclast numbers were not significantly influenced by OVX (Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by histomorphometric analysis data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The absence of M-CSF in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors appears to enable osteoclast lineage cells to be resistant to environmental osteoclastogenic stimuli, such as OVX, thereby mitigating pathologic bone loss.
source: As bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors are a key cell population expressing M-CSF, these results indicate that the absence of M-CSF in these cells appears to enable osteoclast linage cells to be resistant to environmental osteoclastogenic stimuli, such as OVX, thereby mitigating pathologic bone loss.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Csf1∆Adipoq mice show less bone loss and osteoclast formation after OVX.

claim: M-CSF produced by bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors plays an important role in pathologic osteoclastogenesis and bone loss.
source: These data demonstrate an important role for M-CSF produced by bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors in pathologic osteoclastogenesis and bone loss.
evidence: Inferred from the OVX experimental results showing reduced bone loss in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.

claim: M-CSF is a critical growth factor for myeloid lineage cells, including monocytes, macrophages, and osteoclasts.
source: M-CSF is a critical growth factor for myeloid lineage cells, including monocytes, macrophages, and osteoclasts.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge and cited references.

claim: Tissue-resident macrophages in most organs rely on local M-CSF.
source: Tissue-resident macrophages in most organs rely on local M-CSF.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: The global absence of Csf1 in the Csf1op/Csf1op mice leads to tissue macrophage deficiency, growth retardation and skeletal abnormality.
source: The global absence of Csf1 in the Csf1op/ Csf1op mice, which carry an inactivating mutation in the coding region of Csf1, leads to tissue macrophage deficiency, growth retardation and skeletal abnormality.
evidence: Supported by cited references (Cecchini et al., 1994; Dai et al., 2002; Felix et al., 1990; Wiktor-Jedrzejczak et al., 1982; Wiktor-Jedrzejczak et al., 1990; Yoshida et al., 1990).

claim: The severe osteopetrosis, shortened long bones and failure of dental eruption in Csf1op/Csf1op mice attest to the essential role of M-CSF for osteoclast generation.
source: The severe osteopetrosis, shortened long bones and failure of dental eruption in Csf1op/ Csf1op mice attest to the essential role of M-CSF for osteoclast generation (Cecchini et al., 1994; Dai et al., 2002; Felix et al., 1990; Wiktor-Jedrzejczak et al., 1982; Wiktor-Jedrzejczak et al., 1990; Yoshida et al., 1990).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: Osteoclasts are giant multinucleated cells responsible for bone resorption.
source: Osteoclasts are giant multinucleated cells responsible for bone resorption.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Osteoclasts are derived from the monocyte/macrophage lineage and are a specialized terminally differentiated macrophage.
source: They are derived from the monocyte/macrophage lineage and are a specialized terminally differentiated macrophage.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: M-CSF is essential for the entire process of osteoclast differentiation, from the generation of osteoclast precursors to the formation and survival of mature osteoclasts.
source: M-CSF is essential for the entire process of osteoclast differentiation, from the generation of osteoclast precursors to the formation and survival of mature osteoclasts (Ross, 2006; Tanaka et al., 1993; Feng and Teitelbaum, 2013).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: M-CSF acts together with β3 integrin to regulate actin remodeling in osteoclasts to enable osteoclasts to spread, migrate, fuse, and form actin rings to facilitate bone resorption.
source: M-CSF also acts together with β3 integrin to regulate actin remodeling in osteoclasts to enable osteoclasts to spread, migrate, fuse, and form actin rings to facilitate bone resorption (Ross, 2006; Ross and Teitelbaum, 2005; Insogna et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: M-CSF is expressed by a variety of cells, such as endothelial cells, myoblasts, epithelial cells, and fibroblasts.
source: M-CSF is expressed by a variety of cells, such as endothelial cells, myoblasts, epithelial cells, and fibroblasts (Cecchini et al., 1994; Schrader et al., 1991; Clinton et al., 1992; Fibbe et al., 1988).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: Under physiologic conditions, circulating M-CSF is mainly produced by vascular endothelial cells.
source: Under physiologic conditions, circulating M-CSF is mainly produced by vascular endothelial cells (Clinton et al., 1992; Roth and Stanley, 1992; Ryan et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: Macrophages in kidney and liver are highly dependent on circulating M-CSF.
source: For example, macrophages in kidney and liver are highly dependent on circulating M-CSF.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Bone marrow resident macrophages appear to not require circulating M-CSF, indicating the importance of local M-CSF produced in bone marrow.
source: Bone marrow resident macrophages, however, appear to not require circulating M-CSF, indicating the importance of local M-CSF produced in bone marrow (Cecchini et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Osteocytes embedded in bone express M-CSF that contributes to bone mass maintenance.
source: Osteocytes embedded in bone express M-CSF that contributes to bone mass maintenance (Werner et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: In vitro studies show that M-CSF is expressed by an osteoblast cell line, calvarial osteoblastic cells and a cloned bone marrow stromal cell line.
source: Although in vitro studies show that M-CSF is expressed by an osteoblast cell line, calvarial osteoblastic cells and a cloned bone marrow stromal cell line (Tanaka et al., 1993; Elford et al., 1987; Zhao et al., 2002; Naparstek et al., 1986), there is no clear evidence supporting whether osteoblasts express M-CSF in vivo and the contributions of osteoblast-derived M-CSF to macrophage and bone homeostasis in vivo is unclear.
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: There is no clear evidence supporting whether osteoblasts express M-CSF in vivo and the contributions of osteoblast-derived M-CSF to macrophage and bone homeostasis in vivo is unclear.
source: Although in vitro studies show that M-CSF is expressed by an osteoblast cell line, calvarial osteoblastic cells and a cloned bone marrow stromal cell line (Tanaka et al., 1993; Elford et al., 1987; Zhao et al., 2002; Naparstek et al., 1986), there is no clear evidence supporting whether osteoblasts express M-CSF in vivo and the contributions of osteoblast-derived M-CSF to macrophage and bone homeostasis in vivo is unclear.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of clear in vivo evidence despite in vitro studies.

claim: The osteopetrotic phenotype in long bones is similar between Adipoq Cre-driven Csf1 conditional KO mice and RANKL conditional KO mice.
source: The osteopetrotic phenotype in long bones is similar between Adipoq Cre-driven Csf1 (our results) and RANKL conditional KO mice (Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by comparison with cited reference (Yu et al., 2021).

claim: Adipoq Cre-driven RANKL conditional KO mice exhibit osteopetrosis in lumbar bone, while Csf1∆Adipoq mice do not.
source: Interestingly, Adipoq Cre-driven RANKL conditional KO mice also exhibit osteopetrosis in lumbar bone (Yu et al., 2021), while Csf1∆Adipoq mice do not.
evidence: Supported by comparison with cited reference (Yu et al., 2021) and data from this study.

claim: Cells other than Adipoq-expressing cells in lumbar presumably produce sufficient M-CSF or IL34 that could compensate the loss of M-CSF by Adipoq-lineage progenitors.
source: A possibility is that cells other than Adipoq-expressing cells in lumbar presumably produce sufficient M-CSF or IL34 that could compensate the loss of M-CSF by Adipoq-lineage progenitors.
evidence: Speculative explanation for the difference in vertebral bone phenotype.

claim: The difference in vertebral bone phenotype between Csf1∆Adipoq and RANKL conditional KO mice implicates the presence of distinct cellular compartments and microenvironments between long bones and vertebral bones.
source: This difference also implicates the presence of distinct cellular compartments and microenvironments between long bones and vertebral bones.
evidence: Inferred from the observed phenotypic differences.

claim: Adipoq is expressed in mature lipid-laden adipocytes in peripheral adipose tissue but not their progenitors.
source: However, unlike the wide expression of Adipoq in lipid-laden adipocytes to Adipoq-lineage progenitors in bone marrow, Adipoq is expressed in mature lipid-laden adipocytes but not their progenitors in peripheral adipose tissue (Berry and Rodeheffer, 2013).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Peripheral Adipoq+ adipocytes nearly do not produce M-CSF.
source: Additionally, unlike bone marrow Adipoq+ progenitors, these peripheral Adipoq+ cells nearly do not produce M-CSF.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from this study.

claim: Cells producing RANKL usually appear to simultaneously express M-CSF, such as osteocytes and bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors.
source: The cells producing RANKL usually appear to simultaneously express M-CSF, such as osteocytes and bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors (our findings and Werner et al., 2020; Zhong et al., 2020; Yu et al., 2021; Hu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by data from this study and cited references.

claim: Peripheral Adipoq+ adipocytes express neither RANKL nor M-CSF.
source: This is not the case for peripheral Adipoq+ adipocytes, which express neither RANKL (Fan et al., 2017) nor M-CSF (our findings).
evidence: Supported by data from this study and cited reference.

claim: The unique expression of M-CSF and RANKL by bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors is a feature that distinguishes this cell population from other adipose depots.
source: The unique expression of M-CSF and RANKL by bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors is a feature that distinguishes this cell population from other adipose depots.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of expression patterns between bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors and peripheral adipocytes.

claim: Bone marrow macrophages are reduced by approximately half in the Csf1∆Adipoq mice, but macrophages in other tissues/organs are not significantly affected.
source: Bone marrow macrophages are reduced by approximately half in the Csf1∆Adipoq mice, but macrophages in other tissues/organs are not significantly affected.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data from this study.

claim: These results indicate a strong local regulation of macrophage development by bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors via M-CSF.
source: These results indicate a strong local regulation of macrophage development by bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors via M-CSF.
evidence: Inferred from the tissue-specific effects on macrophage populations.

claim: Research using Csf1op/Csf1op mice with the restoration of circulating M-CSF shows that some tissues/organs are dependent much more on local than circulating M-CSF, such as bone marrow.
source: However, research using Csf1op/ Csf1op mice with the restoration of circulating M-CSF shows that some tissues/organs are dependent much more on local than circulating M-CSF, such as bone marrow (Cecchini et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Adipoq-lineage progenitors are a crucial cellular source of M-CSF that controls macrophage and osteoclast populations in bone marrow.
source: Our results support this finding and further demonstrate that Adipoq-lineage progenitors are a crucial cellular source of M-CSF that controls macrophage and osteoclast populations in bone marrow.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental results showing reduced macrophages and osteoclasts in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.

claim: Macrophage development and osteoclastogenesis in bone marrow is more dependent on local M-CSF, presumably a unique mechanism by which bone marrow microenvironment decouples osteoclastogenesis and marrow monocytic development from systemic regulation of tissue-resident macrophages, allowing for marrow homeostasis.
source: It is unclear but interesting why macrophage development and osteoclastogenesis in bone marrow is more dependent on local M-CSF. This is presumably a unique mechanism by which bone marrow microenvironment decouples osteoclastogenesis and marrow monocytic development from systemic regulation of tissue-resident macrophages, allowing for marrow homeostasis.
evidence: Speculative explanation for the observed local dependence on M-CSF.

claim: The deficiency of M-CSF produced by the small Adipoq+ cell population leads to around a 50% increase in trabecular bone mass and an over 50% reduction of bone marrow macrophages.
source: However, the deficiency of M-CSF produced by this small Adipoq+ cell population leads to around a 50% increase in trabecular bone mass and an over 50% reduction of bone marrow macrophages.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from this study.

claim: Adipoq-lineage progenitors are a major cellular source of M-CSF for bone marrow.
source: These results together with the scRNAseq data in Figure 1 demonstrate that Adipoq-lineage progenitor cells in bone marrow produce substantially more M-CSF than osteoblast lineage cells. Thus, Adipoq-lineage progenitors are a major cellular source of M-CSF for bone marrow.
evidence: Inferred from the combination of scRNAseq data and functional studies.

claim: The osteopetrotic phenotype in Csf1∆Adipoq mice is not as strong as Csf1op/Csf1op mice.
source: We also observed that the osteopetrotic phenotype in Csf1∆Adipoq mice is not as strong as Csf1op/ Csf1op mice.
evidence: Inferred from comparison with literature on Csf1op/Csf1op mice.

claim: M-CSF expression was found in cultures of osteoblastic cells, an osteocyte cell line and osteocytes.
source: Literature show that M-CSF expression was found in cultures of osteoblastic cells, an osteocyte cell line and osteocytes (Tanaka et al., 1993; Werner et al., 2020; Elford et al., 1987; Zhao et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: The MSPC-Osteo population expresses Csf1, despite scRNAseq analysis showing that osteoblasts do not express Csf1.
source: Despite scRNAseq analysis showing that osteoblasts do not express Csf1, the MSPC-Osteo population does (Figure 1).
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The M-CSF produced by MSPC-Osteo cells, osteocytes and potentially osteoblasts could partially compensate for the loss of M-CSF from bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitor cells.
source: Collectively, the M-CSF produced by MSPC-Osteo cells, osteocytes and potentially osteoblasts could partially compensate for the loss of M-CSF from bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitor cells.
evidence: Speculative explanation for the incomplete osteopetrotic phenotype in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.

claim: IL34 is an additional ligand for c-Fms and has, at least partially, functional redundancy with M-CSF.
source: IL34 was identified later as an additional ligand for c-Fms. Although it also binds to other receptors aside from c-Fms, IL34 has, at least partially, functional redundancy with M-CSF (Lin et al., 2019; Lelios et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: IL34 is found highly expressed in brain and skin and plays an important role in the differentiation and maintenance of microglia and Langerhans cells.
source: Unlike M-CSF that is broadly and highly expressed by almost every tissue, IL34 is found highly expressed in brain and skin and plays an important role in the differentiation and maintenance of microglia and Langerhans cells (Lin et al., 2019; Lelios et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: The vascular endothelial cells in spleen produce IL34.
source: The vascular endothelial cells in spleen also produce IL34 (Nakamichi et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: IL34 is expressed in bone marrow, largely by Adipoq-lineage progenitors but also moderately by pericytes and slightly by MSPC-Osteo cells.
source: The results from scRNAseq datasets show that IL34 is expressed in bone marrow, largely by Adipoq-lineage progenitors but also moderately by pericytes and slightly by MSPC-Osteo cells (Dolgalev and Tikhonova, 2021).
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data from cited reference.

claim: Adipoq-lineage progenitors are highly likely a major cellular source of IL34 in bone marrow.
source: This indicates that Adipoq-lineage progenitors are highly likely a major cellular source of IL34 in bone marrow.
evidence: Inferred from scRNAseq data showing high IL34 expression in Adipoq-lineage progenitors.

claim: Spleen has a reservoir of RANK+/CSF-1R+ osteoclast precursors, which can home to bone marrow to differentiate to mature osteoclasts in response to RANKL, IL34 and/or M-CSF.
source: Spleen has a reservoir of RANK+/CSF-1R+osteoclast precursors, which can home to bone marrow to differentiate to mature osteoclasts in response to RANKL, IL34 and/or M-CSF (Nakamichi et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Il34 expression in bone marrow is not affected in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: Il34 expression in bone marrow was not affected in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from this study.

claim: IL34 and splenic osteoclast precursors may partially compensate for M-CSF function and alleviate the osteopetrotic and macrophage deficiency phenotype in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
source: These mechanisms collectively may partially compensate for M-CSF function and alleviate the osteopetrotic and macrophage deficiency phenotype in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.
evidence: Speculative explanation for the incomplete phenotype in Csf1∆Adipoq mice.

claim: Adipoq Cre labels other clusters in addition to Adipoq-lineage progenitors, but the expression levels of Adipoq and frequency of Adipoq+ cells in other cell populations are relatively low.
source: In addition to Adipoq-lineage progenitors, Adipoq Cre also labels other clusters. However, the expression levels of Adipoq and frequency of Adipoq+ cells in other cell populations are relatively low.
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data analysis.

claim: Adipoq is expressed at a low level (with scaled mean expression at 0.68) in a small proportion of MSPC-osteo cells.
source: For example, the integrated scRNAseq dataset we analyzed shows that Adipoq is expressed at a low level (with scaled mean expression at 0.68, Dolgalev and Tikhonova, 2021) in a small proportion of MSPC-osteo cells (Figure 1), and small amounts (Yu et al., 2021; Jeffery et al., 2022; about 4%) of osteoblasts in 8 or 12-week-old mice are Adipoq-lineage.
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data from cited references.

claim: Small amounts (about 4%) of osteoblasts in 8 or 12-week-old mice are Adipoq-lineage.
source: For example, the integrated scRNAseq dataset we analyzed shows that Adipoq is expressed at a low level (with scaled mean expression at 0.68, Dolgalev and Tikhonova, 2021) in a small proportion of MSPC-osteo cells (Figure 1), and small amounts (Yu et al., 2021; Jeffery et al., 2022; about 4%) of osteoblasts in 8 or 12-week-old mice are Adipoq-lineage.
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: In 24-week-old mice, about 15-40% of osteoblasts are marked with Adipoq Cre.
source: A recent report found that in 24-week-old mice, about 15–40% of osteoblasts are marked with Adipoq Cre (Jeffery et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: One possibility is that the Adipoq-lineage cells (adipo-CAR cells/MALPs) have minor or latent osteogenic potential that may become more evident under specific conditions, such as in older animals.
source: One possibility is that the Adipoq-lineage cells (adipo-CAR cells/MALPs) have minor or latent osteogenic potential that may become more evident under specific conditions, such as in older animals.
evidence: Speculative explanation for the observed Adipoq-cre labeling in osteoblasts.

claim: An alternative possibility is that Adipoq-cre could primarily target a population of solely adipogenic adipo-CAR cells but that its specificity is imperfect, leading to progressive low levels of deletion in a separate population expressing very low levels of Adipoq, such as osteo-CAR cells.
source: However, balanced against this is the alternative that Adipoq-cre could primarily target a population of solely adipogenic adipo-CAR cells but that its specificity is imperfect, leading to progressive low levels of deletion in a separate population expressing very low levels of Adipoq, such as osteo-CAR cells.
evidence: Speculative alternative explanation for the observed Adipoq-cre labeling in osteoblasts.

claim: An additional possibility is that the Adipoq-lineage cells may themselves actually be further subdivided into multiple component cell types, including a major adipogenic and a separate minor osteogenic subpopulation.
source: An additional possibility is that the Adipoq-lineage cells may themselves actually be further subdivided into multiple component cell types, including a major adipogenic and a separate minor osteogenic subpopulation.
evidence: Speculative alternative explanation for the heterogeneity within Adipoq-lineage cells.

claim: Adipoq cre primarily defines one or possibly more lineages of cells rather than a cell type within those lineages.
source: Ultimately, at the root of these issues is that Adipoq cre primarily defines one or possibly more lineages of cells rather than a cell type within those lineages.
evidence: Inferred from the discussion of Adipoq-cre labeling patterns.

claim: The Adipoq expression level and positive cell proportion are much higher in bone marrow Adipoq lineage progenitors than the levels seen in osteoblast lineage or endothelial cells in bone marrow.
source: Of note, the Adipoq expression level and positive cell proportion are much higher in bone marrow Adipoq lineage progenitors than the levels seen in osteoblast lineage (Figure 1, Figure 2, Zhong et al., 2020; Dolgalev and Tikhonova, 2021; Yu et al., 2021) or endothelial cells in bone marrow (Zhang et al., 2021; Emoto et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data from this study and cited references.

claim: The MSPC-Adipo cluster (Adipoq-lineage progenitors) has 6441 cells with the highest level (scaled mean expression level at 3.01) of Adipoq seen among bone marrow cells analyzed.
source: For example, the MSPC-Adipo cluster (Adipoq-lineage progenitors) has 6441 cells with the highest level (scaled mean expression level at 3.01 per Dolgalev and Tikhonova, 2021 at Single Cell Portal) of Adipoq seen among bone marrow cells analyzed.
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data from cited reference.

claim: The MSPC-osteo cluster consists of 2247 cells with a very low Adipoq expression level (scaled mean expression level at 0.68).
source: In contrast, the MSPC-osteo cluster consists of 2247 cells with a very low Adipoq expression level (scaled mean expression level at 0.68 per Dolgalev and Tikhonova, 2021 at Single Cell Portal).
evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data from cited reference.

claim: The relative overall contribution to Adipoq expression by MSPC-osteo vs the Adipoq-lineage progenitors is 7.8% ([2247x0.68]/[6441x3.01]).
source: Taken together with both average expression level and cell numbers in each cluster, the relative overall contribution to Adipoq expression by MSPC-osteo vs the Adipoq-lineage progenitors is 7.8% ([2247x0.68]/[6441x3.01]).
evidence: Calculated from scRNAseq data.

claim: The expression of Adipoq in MSPC-osteo cluster is marginal compared to that in the Adipoq-lineage progenitors.
source: Therefore, the expression of Adipoq in MSPC-osteo cluster is marginal compared to that in the Adipoq-lineage progenitors.
evidence: Inferred from the quantitative comparison of Adipoq expression.

claim: Adipoq is an important marker to identify bone marrow Adipoq lineage progenitors.
source: These data make Adipoq as an important marker to identify bone marrow Adipoq lineage progenitors.
evidence: Inferred from the high and specific expression of Adipoq in this cell population.

claim: This work validates prior research identifying adipoq-lineage cells, identified as MALPs, as a key osteoclast regulatory population.
source: Overall, our work not only validates prior research identifying adipoq-lineage cells, identified as MALPs (Zhong et al., 2020; Yu et al., 2021), as a key osteoclast regulatory population, but also further extends the scope of their functions to encompass M-CSF production and regulation of macrophages.
evidence: Inferred from the consistency with prior research and new findings.

claim: This work extends the scope of adipoq-lineage cell functions to encompass M-CSF production and regulation of macrophages.
source: Overall, our work not only validates prior research identifying adipoq-lineage cells, identified as MALPs (Zhong et al., 2020; Yu et al., 2021), as a key osteoclast regulatory population, but also further extends the scope of their functions to encompass M-CSF production and regulation of macrophages.
evidence: Inferred from the new findings on M-CSF production and macrophage regulation.

claim: M-CSF is a key factor contributing to pathological bone destruction.
source: In addition to its function in development and postnatal homeostasis, M-CSF is a key factor contributing to pathological bone destruction.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: The extent of bone loss in Csf1∆Adipoq mice is less than that of the control mice in the OVX induced osteoporosis model.
source: In OVX induced osteoporosis model, we found that the extent of bone loss in Csf1∆Adipoq mice was less than that of the control mice, and the bone mass was significantly higher in Csf1∆Adipoq mice than control mice after OVX.
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data from the OVX experiment.

claim: The bone mass is significantly higher in Csf1∆Adipoq mice than control mice after OVX.
source: In OVX induced osteoporosis model, we found that the extent of bone loss in Csf1∆Adipoq mice was less than that of the control mice, and the bone mass was significantly higher in Csf1∆Adipoq mice than control mice after OVX.
evidence: Supported by µCT analysis data from the OVX experiment.

claim: M-CSF produced by Adipoq+ cells plays a significant role in estrogen-deficiency induced bone loss.
source: These results indicate a significant role for the M-CSF produced by Adipoq + cells in estrogen-deficiency induced bone loss.
evidence: Inferred from the OVX experimental results.

claim: No genotype by OVX interaction term was seen in two-way ANOVA.
source: Interestingly, however, no genotype by OVX interaction term was seen in two-way ANOVA, even though there is a significant difference in the post-OVX bone mass between genotypes.
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of the OVX data.

claim: The difference in baseline bone mass pre-OVX between genotypes could presumably complicate and compromise the significance analysis of genotype by OVX interaction.
source: The difference in baseline bone mass pre-OVX between genotypes could presumably complicate and compromise the significance analysis of genotype by OVX interaction.
evidence: Speculative explanation for the lack of interaction term in statistical analysis.

claim: Broad blockade of M-CSF is not clinically feasible because this may suppress macrophage survival and function in a variety of important tissues and organs.
source: Broad blockade of M-CSF, however, is not clinically feasible because this may suppress macrophage survival and function in a variety of important tissues and organs.
evidence: Inferred from the known widespread functions of M-CSF.

claim: Lack of M-CSF in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors does not affect macrophage populations outside of the bone marrow.
source: Our results show that lack of M-CSF in bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors does not affect macrophage populations outside of the bone marrow.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data from this study.

claim: Targeting bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors themselves or the mechanisms regulating their production of M-CSF could be a potential therapeutic strategy to prevent pathological bone destruction.
source: These findings suggest that targeting bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors themselves or the mechanisms regulating their production of M-CSF could be a potential therapeutic strategy to prevent pathological bone destruction.
evidence: Speculative therapeutic implication based on the study findings.

claim: Bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors produce RANKL, an essential cytokine to induce osteoclast differentiation.
source: Bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors also produce RANKL (Yu et al., 2021; Hu et al., 2021), an essential cytokine to induce osteoclast differentiation.
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: These findings collectively highlight the significance of bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors in the regulation of osteoclastogenesis and bone metabolism, as well as the potential translational implications of appropriately targeting this cell population in treating pathologic bone loss.
source: These findings collectively highlight the significance of bone marrow Adipoq-lineage progenitors in the regulation of osteoclastogenesis and bone metabolism, as well as the potential translational implications of appropriately targeting this cell population in treating pathologic bone loss.
evidence: Inferred from the collective findings of the study.
